hypotheses.text: Biallelic SNUPN pathogenic variants cause a phenotypic spectrum ranging from limb-girdle muscular dystrophy to spinocerebellar ataxia, in which cerebellar atrophy is an intrinsic central nervous system manifestation rather than a coincidental finding.
hypotheses.rationale: Initial descriptions classified SNUPN disease as a muscle-restricted limb-girdle muscular dystrophy without central nervous system malformations. However, multiple recent cohorts demonstrate spinocerebellar atrophy, cerebellar ataxia, and neurological defects in patients with pathogenic SNUPN variants, directly contradicting the premise that the disease is confined strictly to skeletal muscle.

evidence.text: Okubo et al. identified pathogenic variants in SNUPN in two families presenting with spinocerebellar atrophy where one patient had mild skeletal muscle changes and the other had none; knock-in mice carrying patient variants developed cerebellar ataxia and cerebellar atrophy.

source.title: SNUPN variants cause spinocerebellar atrophy by disrupting global splicing in cerebellar Purkinje cells
source.quote: We identified pathogenic variants in the SNUPN gene in two families with spinocerebellar atrophy. One patient exhibited mild changes in skeletal muscle, while the other did not... These results expand the clinical spectrum of SNUPN-related disorders beyond skeletal muscle and highlight splicing dysregulation as a potential mechanism underlying cerebellar atrophy.

evidence.text: Nashabat et al. reported 18 children from 15 unrelated families with biallelic hypomorphic SNUPN variants presenting with atypical muscular dystrophy accompanied by neurological defects.

source.title: SNUPN deficiency causes a recessive muscular dystrophy due to RNA mis-splicing and ECM dysregulation
source.quote: In this study, we investigate 18 children from 15 unrelated families who present with atypical muscular dystrophy and neurological defects.

numbers.metric: affected children with muscular dystrophy and neurological defects

evidence.text: Muelas et al. documented that SNUPN-related muscular dystrophy (LGMDR29) covers from congenital/childhood-onset pure muscular dystrophy to complex phenotypes combining neurodevelopmental features, cataracts, or spinocerebellar ataxia.

source.title: SNUPN‐Related Muscular Dystrophy: Novel Phenotypic, Pathological and Functional Protein Insights
source.journal: Annals of Clinical and Translational Neurology
source.quote: SNUPN-related muscular dystrophy or LGMDR29 is a new entity that covers from a congenital or childhood onset pure muscular dystrophy to more complex phenotypes combining neurodevelopmental features, cataracts, or spinocerebellar ataxia.

hypotheses.text: In adult-onset SNUPN-related muscular dystrophy, structural cerebellar atrophy can occur subclinically without overt ataxia or intellectual impairment.
hypotheses.rationale: Early probands evaluated for isolated limb-girdle muscular dystrophy were believed to lack central nervous system involvement. However, systematic brain imaging in adult-onset siblings demonstrated structural cerebellar atrophy in an asymptomatic individual, showing that cerebellar involvement may be radiologically present even when clinical ataxia or cognitive deficit is absent.

evidence.text: In a family with two siblings displaying adult-onset proximo-distal and axial muscle weakness due to novel SNUPN variants (p.Arg27Cys and p.Cys174Tyr), one sibling presented with asymptomatic cerebellar atrophy on brain MRI.

source.title: SNUPN‐Related Muscular Dystrophy: Novel Phenotypic, Pathological and Functional Protein Insights
source.journal: Annals of Clinical and Translational Neurology
source.quote: Two siblings carrying two novel deleterious variants in the SNUPN gene (p.Arg27Cys and p.Cys174Tyr) showed adult-onset proximo-distal and axial muscle weakness with early respiratory involvement. One patient presented with asymptomatic cerebellar atrophy.

evidence.text: Liewluck summarizes LGMDR29 as presenting with or without myofibrillar pathology and with cerebellar atrophy as an associated feature.

source.title: Limb-girdle muscular dystrophies
source.quote: SNUPN No distinctive neuromuscular features With or without myofibrillar pathology Cerebellar atrophy…

hypotheses.text: The distinction between isolated limb-girdle muscular dystrophy and spinocerebellar ataxia in SNUPN-related disease is governed by cell-type-specific vulnerability to U1 snRNP mis-splicing rather than mutually exclusive variant categories.
hypotheses.rationale: Purkinje cells and skeletal muscle fibers both rely on SNUPN-dependent U1 snRNP nuclear transport, but Purkinje cell dendritic development and sonic hedgehog secretion depend heavily on global splicing fidelity, enabling single SNUPN mutations to produce varying severity ratios of cerebellar degeneration versus skeletal myopathy.

evidence.text: Purkinje cells in knock-in mice carrying patient SNUPN variants exhibited impaired U1 snRNP nuclear transport, abnormal RNA splicing in genes related to neuronal development, dendritic abnormalities, and reduced sonic hedgehog secretion, while one human patient with spinocerebellar atrophy exhibited mild muscle alterations and another had none.

source.title: SNUPN variants cause spinocerebellar atrophy by disrupting global splicing in cerebellar Purkinje cells
source.quote: Mutated snurportin-1 displayed impaired nuclear transport and reduced binding to importin beta. The knock-in mouse mimicking the compound heterozygous variants exhibited cerebellar ataxia, cerebellar atrophy and dendritic abnormalities in Purkinje cells... These results expand the clinical spectrum of SNUPN-related disorders beyond skeletal muscle and highlight splicing dysregulation as a potential mechanism underlying cerebellar atrophy.

new_directions.question_text: What is the exact penetrance of cerebellar atrophy on brain MRI across all documented molecularly confirmed SNUPN cohorts, and does it correlate with age of onset or specific variant domains?
new_directions.rationale: Resolving whether brain MRI should be mandatory in every patient evaluated for suspected LGMDR29 requires quantifying how many probands with limb weakness have subclinical or clinical cerebellar changes.

new_directions.question_text: Does SNUPN deficiency cause true intellectual disability or primary cardiac conduction defects, or are these features strictly absent, thereby cleanly differentiating LGMDR29 from dystroglycanopathies and Emery-Dreifuss syndromes?
new_directions.rationale: Clarifying the negative findings (such as absence of primary cardiomyopathy or major brain structural malformations beyond cerebellar atrophy) will define key exclusion criteria for clinicians facing overlapping myopathies.
